title: Storyblocks Pricing 2026: Plans & Costs After Free Trial
summary: Storyblocks pricing depends on how many videos you download and who watches them. Find the plan that fits your project scope and team needs.
body_markdown:
## Automating Storyblocks downloads and client handoff with Activepieces


Activepieces won't change anything about what Storyblocks charges you. It is an automation tool with an MIT-licensed core and 747 integrations, among them the forms, spreadsheets, email and cloud storage this workflow uses.


It can record every download and licence as it happens, so you see which limit your work is hitting before the invoice or the cap tells you.


Activepieces' own pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, whatever the number of steps, against Zapier's per-task billing on its pricing page, so the four per-project steps below cost the same as a two-step version, and the free plan's 1,000 credits a month cover 1,000 of those runs.


Once you know your monthly output, a short workflow keeps that count honest.


The flow runs in this order:


1. Trigger on a new form submission or a new row in a Google Sheets tracker.
2. Log the asset ID and licence type.
3. Send the client handoff email.
4. Create and file the Google Drive folder.
5. Run the Monday plan limits audit.


You can see where each step sits in the sequence below: the first four run per project and only the last runs weekly, which means you'll complete four steps during project setup, then manage one recurring weekly task.


### Stage 1: capture the asset list


Start with a trigger that fires whenever someone on your team adds an asset. It can be either a short form (asset URL or ID, project name, client name) or a new row in a Sheets tracker. Pick one and make it mandatory.


If editors can download without filling it in, the log will undercount, and an undercounted log is exactly how you drift past a download limit without noticing.


Activepieces reads each submission as a single run, and a run is 1 credit however many steps follow, so one asset per row keeps the record clean at 1 credit apiece.


### Stage 2: log licence details


Next, have the flow write the asset ID and the licence type into a master sheet, one line per asset, with the date and the project. The licence column matters more than it looks.


Whether a clip is covered for client work or a monetized channel is what decides if you can hand it over. A separate record means you can answer a client's licence question later without searching your download history.


The log also gives you real counts by month, which is the number you needed when comparing plans.


### Stage 3: send the client handoff


Add a step that sends the client an email listing the assets used, their licence type and a link to the project folder. Then create the Drive folder, named by client and project, and file the delivered assets and the email's contents inside it.


Your licence doesn't change because Activepieces moved information between tools: Essentials stays a one-user plan at $21 a month billed annually, however many flows run on top of it. That is the honest limit here.


If a licence type on the sheet doesn't cover the client's use, the automation will happily send the email anyway. Add a check that flags any row whose licence is blank or unexpected before the email goes out.


### Weekly Storyblocks download and licence check


Each Monday, filter the master sheet for the past week and compare it to your plan's download and licence limits.


Check three things: how many downloads you logged, whether any licence types appeared that your plan doesn't cover for client work, and whether the weekly pace projects past the monthly cap. If it does, that's the signal to move plans.
